name: May Fourth Movement
title: The story of the May Fourth Movement

text: More than 100 years ago, after President Yuan Shikai died, warlords ruled much of China.
The government in Beijing could do little against powerful foreign countries.
src: After the death of President Yuan Shikai in 1916 China was dominated by warlords
the government in Beijing could do little against foreign influence

text: After the First World War, a peace treaty gave Germany's rights in Shandong, a part of China, to Japan.
Many in China felt betrayed, because China had sent 140,000 workers to help the Allies in the war.
src: the Treaty of Versailles awarded the rights to the German territories in Shandong, surrendered by Germany after the Siege of Tsingtao in 1914, to Japan
China had entered World War I on the side of the Triple Entente in 1917 and sent 140,000 labourers to the Western Front / was seen as a betrayal

text: On the fourth of May, over 4,000 students gathered in front of Tiananmen in Beijing to protest.
When nearly 1,000 students were arrested, workers and shopkeepers stopped work to support them.
src: On May 4, 1919, over 4,000 students marched to Tiananmen against the Treaty of Versailles’ award
When the government arrested nearly 1,000 students in June, workers and merchants struck in their support

text: The government sacked three officials, and China refused to sign the treaty, though Japan kept Shandong for a while.
Many Chinese stopped trusting Western promises, such as President Wilson's Fourteen Points.
src: the government dismissed the three officials and China’s delegation refused to sign the treaty, but Japan for the moment kept control of the Shandong Peninsula
saw Wilson’s Fourteen Points as hypocritical

text: Writers began to write the way people spoke, instead of in the old formal Chinese.
Lu Xun and Chen Hengzhe wrote some of the first stories in everyday Chinese.
src: Writers were urged to write as they spoke / written vernacular Chinese gained currency over Literary Chinese
Chen Hengzhe and Lu Xun, writers of early vernacular fiction

text: Two of its leaders, Chen Duxiu and Li Dazhao, helped found the Chinese Communist Party.
Today the fourth of May is celebrated as Youth Day in China.
src: Chen Duxiu and Li Dazhao are among the founders of the Chinese Communist Party
May 4 is celebrated as Youth Day in China and as Literary Day in Taiwan
